lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Move Technical Skills near the top.
items.because: Recruiters and ATS systems should see relevant skills quickly.

items.says: Put Experience in reverse chronological order, with the internship first.
items.because: The internship is more recent than the junior engineer role.

items.says: Move Education after Experience and Projects.
items.because: The résumé has substantial experience and relevant projects.

items.says: Remove manual line breaks that split words such as “on-call.”
items.because: They can render awkwardly in ATS systems and PDFs.

items.says: Keep verb tense consistent between past work and ongoing work.
items.because: Past roles and completed projects should use past tense, while ongoing work should use present tense.

items.says: Standardize punctuation across the bullets.
Make sure the code link leads directly to a polished GitHub profile or portfolio.
items.because: It should not lead to a generic or indirect page.

items.says: Add LinkedIn if you use it professionally.
Add GPA or relevant coursework only if it strengthens the application.
items.because: It should be relevant to the target role.

items.says: Clarify the scope of dashboard and on-call ownership.
items.because: The wording does not make clear whether you maintained the dashboards, participated in the rotation, or were responsible for both.

items.says: Make clear that the load-test conditions are representative, if space allows.
items.because: That gives the 200 ms threshold meaning.

items.says: Clarify how much the regression checks contributed to the shorter release cycle.
items.because: They may have been one part of a broader change.

items.says: Separate or prioritize the migration bullet’s contributions.
items.because: Migration, logging work, onboarding, on-call ownership, and the dispatch outcome bury the main contribution.

items.says: Clarify whether onboarding and on-call work belonged to the migration initiative.
items.because: They may have been separate responsibilities.

items.says: Clarify what “triage branch” means.
items.because: It could sound like a code branch rather than a product feature or system component.

items.says: Specify the backlog reduction’s comparison period or baseline if substantiated.
items.because: The 68% result needs a clear comparison.

items.says: Call the accuracy change an 8 percentage-point improvement.
items.because: That makes the change from 71% to 79% clear.

items.says: Prioritize technical terminology for the target role.
items.because: The adapter, trajectory, and loss-masking details may be dense for a general SWE audience.

items.says: Explain how dynamic batching applies to the single-request measurement.
items.because: Those details may seem at odds to a reader.

items.says: Include hardware or serving context if useful.
items.because: It would make the latency result more interpretable.

items.says: Simplify the sentence structure and training-detail list.
items.because: They obscure the result.

items.says: Clarify what changed and what the 5% result measures.
items.because: The end-to-end latency claim is difficult to follow.

items.says: Explain how the 5% end-to-end result relates to the inference-latency result above.
items.because: The two latency results are presented separately.

items.says: Add measurable evidence that training was “stabilised.”
items.because: Readers may not know what improved.

items.says: Use spelling consistent with the rest of the résumé.
items.because: “Stabilised” is UK spelling, while the rest reads more like US English.

items.says: Include a concrete effect of the runbook if there was one.
items.because: Its stated impact is currently only adoption, which may be less valuable than stronger technical bullets.

items.says: Replace the broad “AI-first” claim with concrete practices, systems, or adoption evidence.
items.because: The claim is difficult to verify and does not say what you built.

items.says: Explain what “improving outcomes” means.
items.because: The claimed outcome is vague.

items.says: The stated 50% latency reduction is incorrect.
items.because: A drop from 900 ms to 600 ms is a 33% reduction.

items.says: Specify what the tool-call latency measurement covers.
items.because: “Tool-call latency” could be interpreted in more than one way.

items.says: Describe the benchmark or evaluation conditions.
items.because: Readers need to understand what the 12% refers to.

items.says: Tie the retry strategy clearly to the measured improvement.
items.because: The attribution should be clear.

items.says: Identify what the metrics assess, if there is room.
items.because: The current claim describes adoption but not the metrics’ purpose.

items.says: State what the correlation is between.
items.because: The evaluator score and measure of injected degradation are needed to interpret 0.89.

items.says: Describe the defects’ nature or consequences more specifically.
items.because: “Stability, sourcing and parameter handling” is broad.

items.says: Clarify what changed after the defects were fixed.
Expand the skills inventory with technologies demonstrated in the experience, if you can discuss them confidently.
items.because: The résumé mentions several methods and systems, but Skills lists only a few items; a fuller inventory can improve ATS matching.

items.says: Separate programming languages from tools such as Git.
items.because: Distinct languages, frameworks, methods, and tools are easier to scan.

items.says: Move Kubernetes to a cloud or infrastructure category.
items.because: It does not belong under “ML & Agents.”

items.says: Separate methods such as LoRA and GRPO from tools and frameworks.
items.because: Putting methods and tools in one category makes Skills harder to scan.
